newsitem.title: UK: UBS raises FTSE 100 year-end target to 4,600.
newsitem.headline: UBS raises FTSE 100 year-end target to 4,600.

text.p: UBS on Monday raised its current year-end FTSE 100 target to 4,600 from 4,300 in line with a reduction in gilt yield forecasts.
UBS also raised its 1998 FTSE target to 5,000 from 4,750, strategist Mark Tinker said.
"As a result of an independent Bank of England it has reduced the risk premium on all UK assets and what is good for gilts is good for equities," Tinker said.
"We have brought down our central gilts target and as a result we are still happy with the earnings being generated by UK equities."
Tinker cut his ten year gilt yield forecast to 7.5 percent.

"So I think the market is rationally exuberant at this level," he commented. "It was starting to look expensive and it certainly shouldn't have rallied merely on the Labour victory, but the independent Bank of England justifies it."
